newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague breweries says H1 revenue rises.
newsitem.headline: Prague breweries says H1 revenue rises.

text.p: First-half 1997 revenue at Prague-based brewer Prazske Pivovary a.s., majority owned by Bass Plc, rose to 1.161 billion crowns from 1.01 reported for the same period last year, the company said in a statement.

Profit and loss results were not disclosed. Prazske Pivovary said total sales by volume fell by two percent, year-on-year to 1.239 million hectolitres of beer, but export sales by volume were up 20 percent to 207,000 hectolitres.

"Despite poor weather in June, we are pleased with our second quarter results. The wholesale price increase in March has led to pressure on volumes, but we now feel our brands are properly positioned against the competition," said Prazske Pivovary chief executive Graham Staley.
The statement said the largest growth in sales was for the Staropramen and Branik brands which accounted for 61 percent of domestic sales volumes.
Sales of the flagship label Staropramen rose 15 percent, while sales of Branik were up 78 percent, it said.
"Our regional brands remain under competitive pressure," Staley said.
It added that the introduction of import quotas on beer in the Czech Republic's former federation partner Slovakia was "disappointing".
"Staropramen has enjoyed success in that market, competing on quality and not price."

Bass took a 33 percent stake in Prazske Pivovary in 1994 and gradually increased its holdings to the current 55 percent. Along the way, Bass bought up two small regional breweries merging them into Prazske Pivovary earlier this year.

The British brewer also has a 33 percent stake in the Czech Republic's second largest brewery, Radegast a.s., and would also like to increase its holding. Radegast revenue was not included in Friday's statement.
